principles: Consume already-resolved gitRoot resolvers (resolveDoctorGitCwd / resolveGitCwd); never add a new gitRoot resolution path.
Plain-repo behavior must stay byte-identical: gitCwd defaults to root/projectRoot, and the rebase is identity when gitCwd==projectRoot.
Keep the git-diff base and the tsconfig-relativity base consistent: rebase gitRoot-relative diff paths to projectRoot-relative so computeOutOfScopeTsconfigs matches on a single base.
Mirror the existing scan-function param style (optional gitCwd defaulting to root) for minimal surface.
Use DI seams for tests; never spawn real git where a reader/cwd injection already exists.
drivers: doctor --repair on wrapper-root currently returns wrote:false because repairStoryMetadataAllowlist git rev-parse runs in metadataRoot (not a git repo).
lint change-scope on wrapper-root silently falls back to full recursive tsc because git diff runs in metadataRoot and throws -> resolveChangedFiles returns undefined.
The two fixes are the last B-1637/B-2856 stacking gaps confirmed by combination review.

options.name: A-thread-and-rebase
pros: repairStoryMetadataAllowlist gets an optional gitCwd (mirrors the 3 scan fns); call site passes the gitProbeCwd already resolved at doctor.ts:63.
resolveChangedFiles/defaultChangedFilesReader get an optional gitCwd; call sites pass the gitCwd already resolved at verifier.ts:604 / review-preflight.ts:262.
Rebasing gitRoot-relative paths to projectRoot-relative keeps computeOutOfScopeTsconfigs on a single consistent base (no skip-all misclassification).
Identity rebase when gitCwd==projectRoot -> plain repos byte-identical.
Fully testable via DI (gitCwd param + injectable changedFilesReader).
cons: Touches 4 files + adds a rebase step that must be carefully proven identity in the plain case.

options.name: B-switch-tsconfig-base
pros: Avoids per-path rebase; one base switch.
cons: Would require changing findTsconfigs + computeOutOfScopeTsconfigs relativity base from projectRoot to gitRoot — a far larger blast radius touching code B-1637/B-2856 already stabilized.
Risks regressing plain-repo + every other consumer of those fns; violates the do-not-touch-already-fixed-sites constraint.

rationale: Option A is the minimal, consistency-preserving change: it only consumes the already-resolved gitCwd at the two lagging call sites and rebases diff paths so the single projectRoot relativity base in computeOutOfScopeTsconfigs is preserved. Option B would enlarge the blast radius into already-stabilized B-1637/B-2856 code and risk plain-repo regressions, violating the do-not-touch constraint.

preMortem.scenario: Base mismatch: git diff switched to gitRoot but diff paths NOT rebased
preMortem.trigger: Implementer threads gitCwd into the reader but forgets to rebase the emitted paths to projectRoot-relative.
preMortem.consequence: On wrapper-root, every changed file maps to zero projectRoot tsconfig subtrees -> fail-closed branch treats all as in-scope (full tsc) or misclassifies the skip set.
preMortem.mitigation: resolveChangedFiles rebases each gitRoot-relative path via relative(projectRoot, join(gitCwd, path)); add a wrapper-root regression test asserting the out-of-scope set, plus a plain-repo test asserting identical output to today.

preMortem.trigger: gitCwd param defaulting wrong (undefined instead of root) makes git rev-parse run in cwd:undefined.
preMortem.consequence: repairStoryMetadataAllowlist throws or runs in process cwd, breaking the allowlist install on every plain repo.
preMortem.mitigation: Default the new param to root (gitCwd: string = root), exactly like the 3 scan fns; add a plain-repo --repair test asserting wrote-then-noop behavior is unchanged.

preMortem.trigger: A future refactor returns null/undefined from the resolver.
preMortem.consequence: git commands run in an undefined cwd and throw, turning a graceful fallback into a hard failure.
preMortem.mitigation: Both call sites pass the already-coalesced value; inside resolveChangedFiles/repair, coalesce gitCwd ?? projectRoot/root before use; tests inject undefined gitCwd and assert fallback.

preMortem.scenario: Empty change-scope vs failed change-scope confusion after rebase
preMortem.trigger: Rebase or normalization accidentally drops all paths, producing [] instead of undefined.
preMortem.consequence: [] is a VALID scope (nothing changed) -> computeOutOfScopeTsconfigs marks ALL tsconfigs out-of-scope and skips everything (skip-all) — the exact failure the undefined sentinel prevents.
preMortem.mitigation: Preserve the contract: reader throw -> undefined (full tsc); only a genuinely empty diff yields []. Rebase happens after the throw/normalize boundary and never converts a thrown read into []. Add a test: throwing reader -> undefined, empty-diff reader -> [] unchanged.
